same_type_textbook_practice.title: Classify quadratic roots without solving
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Substitute the specified coefficient value if necessary, evaluate the numerical discriminant and state the number/nature of real roots. No root-solving or parameter-set proof is requested.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Prove a parameter-universal root claim
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Prove a parameterised quadratic always has real roots by showing its discriminant is positive; source Try Now20(b) uses 3x² + 2qx - 3k². Preserve the exam non-zero restriction for distinctness; the source two-parameter extension may include equality.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Prove a parameter-universal root claim
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: For integer parameters, establish a perfect-square discriminant (or equivalent factorisation), then justify rational roots with a non-zero leading coefficient. Source Try Now19(a) has integer p and k; the exam has one non-zero integer k.

The exam intermediate is e^x and is inverted logarithmically, rather than solving a second rational-to-quadratic equation.

The exam sets K=x² and recovers signed square roots, not solutions of 2x+1/x=K.

The exam must select arcs at two different radii, exclude the internal radial lengths and add only the two exposed straight pieces before simplifying a symbolic perimeter. The source lacks the composite boundary selection.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Infer sector angle/radius from area or boundary information

textbook_structural_branches.title: Read an annular sector and identify all exposed boundaries
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The source constructs an outer radius from radial width, infers the common angle and traces two same-angle arcs plus two width edges. The exam instead joins a minor outer sector to a complementary major inner sector, so its inner arc uses 2pi-alpha rather than alpha. The source adds angle inference; the exam adds complementary-major boundary selection.

The source adds trigonometric reconstruction/area, while the exam adds two-radius arc selection and symbolic simplification.

candidate_decisions.rejection_reason: 8227:EXAM:2021:P1:Q7:b asks: (b) In the case where r = 5 cm and α = 0.8, find the area of the metal plate. same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Selected i-displacement forms MN=ON-OM from numerical positions, exactly as the isolated exam part forms AB=OB-OA. Position-vector and geometric-interpretation responses in the same example are excluded.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Read directed arrows and form position/displacement components
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The selected source forms one displacement from two positions. The exam additionally multiplies AB by 3/2 and translates from A to an external point P; those signed section and translation decisions are absent from the source.
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_scope: supporting assessed subtask; not the complete exam task
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The selected source forms one displacement from two positions. The exam additionally multiplies AB by 3/2 and translates from A to an external point P; those signed section and translation decisions are absent from the source.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Read directed arrows and form position/displacement components
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: Both use an endpoint difference, but the source endpoints are supplied numerical coordinates. In the pyramid exam N must first be inferred as the midpoint of BV using the dimensions and apex height, before AN is formed.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: Both use an endpoint difference, but the source endpoints are supplied numerical coordinates. In the pyramid exam N must first be inferred as the midpoint of BV using the dimensions and apex height, before AN is formed.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Read directed arrows and form position/displacement components
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The source explicitly supplies both endpoint positions, whereas the exam requires reading A and C from the oriented rectangular-base diagram before forming the diagonal AC. The subtraction response is shared; the source omits the spatial interpretation.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The source explicitly supplies both endpoint positions, whereas the exam requires reading A and C from the oriented rectangular-base diagram before forming the diagonal AC. The subtraction response is shared; the source omits the spatial interpretation.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Use a division ratio to recover relative basis displacements
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: Both choose a fractional displacement and add an origin path to locate a point. The source uses an internal E-to-F ratio 2:1 in an abstract triangle basis; the exam uses AP=(3/2)AB outside the segment and numerical Cartesian positions. External signed weights add a decision absent from the source.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: Both choose a fractional displacement and add an origin path to locate a point. The source uses an internal E-to-F ratio 2:1 in an abstract triangle basis; the exam uses AP=(3/2)AB outside the segment and numerical Cartesian positions. External signed weights add a decision absent from the source.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Use a division ratio to recover relative basis displacements
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: Source (a) first takes DF-DE to obtain EF in an abstract basis and then scales it by 2/3 to form EG. The isolated exam part asks only for OB-OA. The source includes an extra given-ratio scaling response.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: Source (a) first takes DF-DE to obtain EF in an abstract basis and then scales it by 2/3 to form EG. The isolated exam part asks only for OB-OA. The source includes an extra given-ratio scaling response.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Use a division ratio to recover relative basis displacements
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: Both locate a fractional point on an edge and obtain a directed vector by adding/subtracting positions. The source uses an abstract planar 2:1 triangle division; the exam first infers a three-dimensional apex and a BV midpoint from dimensions, then forms AN. The source omits those spatial-coordinate decisions.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: Both locate a fractional point on an edge and obtain a directed vector by adding/subtracting positions. The source uses an abstract planar 2:1 triangle division; the exam first infers a three-dimensional apex and a BV midpoint from dimensions, then forms AN. The source omits those spatial-coordinate decisions.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Recover hidden spatial positions and sloping edge lengths
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: Both interpret a raised roof/pyramid point from base dimensions and height and form a displacement. The source roof has a centred ridge of known length and asks for several edges; the exam uses an apex above the base centre and a midpoint of BV before AN. The spatial construction differs rather than only the numbers.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: Both interpret a raised roof/pyramid point from base dimensions and height and form a displacement. The source roof has a centred ridge of known length and asks for several edges; the exam uses an apex above the base centre and a midpoint of BV before AN. The spatial construction differs rather than only the numbers.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Recover hidden spatial positions and sloping edge lengths
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The source (a)–(b) chain reads roof vertices and returns several spatial edges; the isolated exam part reads two rectangular-base vertices and returns their diagonal. The source adds the centred-ridge coordinate decisions.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The source (a)–(b) chain reads roof vertices and returns several spatial edges; the isolated exam part reads two rectangular-base vertices and returns their diagonal. The source adds the centred-ridge coordinate decisions.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Recover hidden spatial positions and sloping edge lengths
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The source constructs roof coordinates and endpoint differences for four edges. The exam directly subtracts two supplied positions for AB, without interpreting a spatial model.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The source constructs roof coordinates and endpoint differences for four edges. The exam directly subtracts two supplied positions for AB, without interpreting a spatial model.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Recover internal,external and midpoint positions
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: Both locate a point on the line through two supplied positions. The source uses an internal 2:3 division, with positive convex weights; the exam has AP=(3/2)AB, so P lies beyond B and the A weight is negative. The source omits that external-division sign decision.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: Both locate a point on the line through two supplied positions. The source uses an internal 2:3 division, with positive convex weights; the exam has AP=(3/2)AB, so P lies beyond B and the A weight is negative. The source omits that external-division sign decision.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Recover internal,external and midpoint positions
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The source forms a position from two endpoints and a given internal ratio. The exam instead supplies A and the midpoint B through AB=BC and recovers the missing endpoint C=2B-A. Reversing the section relation adds the unknown-endpoint decision.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The source forms a position from two endpoints and a given internal ratio. The exam instead supplies A and the midpoint B through AB=BC and recovers the missing endpoint C=2B-A. Reversing the section relation adds the unknown-endpoint decision.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Find a midpoint position vector
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The selected source averages two supplied endpoint positions to locate their midpoint. The exam locates an external section point with multiplier 3/2, requiring signed unequal weights rather than the fixed internal 1/2 weights.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The selected source averages two supplied endpoint positions to locate their midpoint. The exam locates an external section point with multiplier 3/2, requiring signed unequal weights rather than the fixed internal 1/2 weights.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Find a midpoint position vector
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The selected source finds the midpoint from both endpoints. The exam supplies A and midpoint B through AB=BC and asks for the missing endpoint C, so it must reverse the averaging relation rather than apply it forwards.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The selected source finds the midpoint from both endpoints. The exam supplies A and midpoint B through AB=BC and asks for the missing endpoint C, so it must reverse the averaging relation rather than apply it forwards.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Recover a missing parallelogram vertex from three position vectors

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Construct tangent and normal equations at a curve point
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Example12 and the target differentiate an explicit algebraic sum of powers at a supplied full point, take the negative reciprocal gradient and return the normal equation. The reciprocal and polynomial coefficients/point values change; there is no unknown-contact search in either.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Recover a tangent point from a further incidence condition
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The source imposes that the tangent at unknown p to (4-x)*exp(x) passes through the origin, equating its derivative with a secant/incidence slope. The target instead supplies tangent slope -9 and recovers the quartic contact point/intercept. Unknown contact is shared, but point-incidence versus prescribed-slope equations and product-exponential versus polynomial differentiation differ.

same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Goldie Q11(i) proves integral 6 to 16 of 6/(2x-7) equals ln(125). The exam proves integral 1 to 4 of 8/(2x+1) equals ln(81). Both recognise the scaled reciprocal-affine primitive, subtract the endpoints and combine logarithms to the supplied exact target; only coefficients/bounds change.

textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The source evaluates a known polynomial at one divisor root to obtain its remainder. The exam reverses the givens: two remainders are supplied and two unknown coefficients must be recovered jointly.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The source evaluates a known polynomial at one divisor root to obtain its remainder. The exam reverses the givens: two remainders are supplied and two unknown coefficients must be recovered jointly.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Evaluate a remainder or prove a supplied factor

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Factor a polynomial then recover roots of a composed expression
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Both first divide p by x+2 with a nonzero remainder, then use that result to factor the adjusted polynomial p minus that remainder. The source uses p-5 and the exam p+5; the prior quotient becomes the residual quadratic in both.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Search admissible rational/integer roots and decide what failure means
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: Spotting one integer root is an initial stage only; the exam continues to the residual quadratic and all three real roots, including fractional roots.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: Spotting one integer root is an initial stage only; the exam continues to the residual quadratic and all three real roots, including fractional roots.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Search admissible rational/integer roots and decide what failure means
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The source has to choose and test integer candidates to discover a root. The exam obtains its first factor directly from the preceding quotient/remainder result.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The source has to choose and test integer candidates to discover a root. The exam obtains its first factor directly from the preceding quotient/remainder result.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Search admissible rational/integer roots and decide what failure means
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The source stops after finding an integer polynomial root; the exam must complete factorisation and recover all bounded trig angles from a transformed polynomial.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The source stops after finding an integer polynomial root; the exam must complete factorisation and recover all bounded trig angles from a transformed polynomial.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Factor a polynomial over the admitted real domain
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: Both discover a rational factor and split the residual quadratic, but the source ends with a factorisation while the exam additionally requires every real root. Keep the zero-product/root-list output explicit.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: Both discover a rational factor and split the residual quadratic, but the source ends with a factorisation while the exam additionally requires every real root. Keep the zero-product/root-list output explicit.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Factor a polynomial over the admitted real domain
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: Both return complete cubic factors, but the source must discover an initial rational root; the exam can infer its initial factor and quadratic quotient from the preceding nonzero-remainder identity for p+5.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: Both return complete cubic factors, but the source must discover an initial rational root; the exam can infer its initial factor and quadratic quotient from the preceding nonzero-remainder identity for p+5.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Factor a polynomial over the admitted real domain
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The factorisation stage is shared. The exam continues to a reciprocal-trig substitution, rejects impossible ratios and enumerates the strict doubled-angle interval; the source stops at polynomial factors.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The factorisation stage is shared. The exam continues to a reciprocal-trig substitution, rejects impossible ratios and enumerates the strict doubled-angle interval; the source stops at polynomial factors.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Factor a polynomial then recover roots of a composed expression
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The source first factors an adjusted polynomial then solves p(|x|)-5=0, retaining nonnegative intermediate roots and recovering both signs. The exam solves the plain cubic without that original-variable recovery.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The source first factors an adjusted polynomial then solves p(|x|)-5=0, retaining nonnegative intermediate roots and recovering both signs. The exam solves the plain cubic without that original-variable recovery.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Factor a polynomial then recover roots of a composed expression
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The book factors the supplied polynomial and solves its single-angle composition. The exam must first recognise the offset polynomial f+6 from the preceding remainder and then solve a cosecant equation in a doubled angle over the stated range. Those decisions are absent from the book selection.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The book factors the supplied polynomial and solves its single-angle composition. The exam must first recognise the offset polynomial f+6 from the preceding remainder and then solve a cosecant equation in a doubled angle over the stated range. Those decisions are absent from the book selection.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Test or prove a supplied polynomial factor
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The source proves a specified factor by one zero evaluation. The exam supplies no factor and requires discovering one, factoring the residual quadratic and reporting every cubic root.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The source proves a specified factor by one zero evaluation. The exam supplies no factor and requires discovering one, factoring the residual quadratic and reporting every cubic root.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Test or prove a supplied polynomial factor
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The factor is given as a condition in the exam, where it combines with a second polynomial remainder to recover unknown coefficients. The source instead knows all coefficients and proves the proposed factor.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The factor is given as a condition in the exam, where it combines with a second polynomial remainder to recover unknown coefficients. The source instead knows all coefficients and proves the proposed factor.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Test or prove a supplied polynomial factor
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The source is a direct supplied-factor proof. The exam must infer a factor of p+5 from the previous nonzero remainder and then factorise that adjusted cubic completely.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The source is a direct supplied-factor proof. The exam must infer a factor of p+5 from the previous nonzero remainder and then factorise that adjusted cubic completely.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Test or prove a supplied polynomial factor
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The exam infers and completes a factorisation of f+6, then filters and solves a cosecant-double-angle equation on a strict interval. The source only establishes one supplied factor.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The exam infers and completes a factorisation of f+6, then filters and solves a cosecant-double-angle equation on a strict interval. The source only establishes one supplied factor.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Test or prove a supplied polynomial factor
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The exam uses the supplied factor and a nonzero remainder as two equations for unknown coefficients; the source knows those coefficients and verifies only the zero-remainder factor claim.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The exam uses the supplied factor and a nonzero remainder as two equations for unknown coefficients; the source knows those coefficients and verifies only the zero-remainder factor claim.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Test or prove a supplied polynomial factor
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: This selected member verifies a complete quadratic factor, for which one zero evaluation is insufficient; the supplied linear-factor exemplar needs only one. The exam instead completes a cubic factorisation from its preceding quotient relation.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: This selected member verifies a complete quadratic factor, for which one zero evaluation is insufficient; the supplied linear-factor exemplar needs only one. The exam instead completes a cubic factorisation from its preceding quotient relation.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Recover coefficients from factor and remainder constraints
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Both use two distinct linear-divisor remainder conditions on one cubic to form and solve two linear equations for its unknown coefficients. The locations of those coefficients and the numeric remainder values vary.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Recover coefficients from factor and remainder constraints
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: The two cubic definitions have the same shared-parameter structure in both sources. One factor condition on f and one nonzero remainder on g give a joint linear system for a,b; only the factor input and remainder value change.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Recover coefficients from factor and remainder constraints
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Both supply one linear factor and one nonzero remainder for a cubic with two unknown coefficients. Translate the factor into value zero, use the second divisor root and solve the two correlated linear constraints.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Recover coefficients from factor and remainder constraints
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: This member has one unknown coefficient and one remainder condition, so a single linear equation suffices; the exam/exemplar requires two jointly recovered coefficients.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: This member has one unknown coefficient and one remainder condition, so a single linear equation suffices; the exam/exemplar requires two jointly recovered coefficients.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Recover coefficients from factor and remainder constraints
textbook_structural_branches.comparison_evidence: The source poses two independent one-coefficient calculations, not one simultaneous two-coefficient system. Each remainder condition must remain attached to its own original polynomial.
textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The source poses two independent one-coefficient calculations, not one simultaneous two-coefficient system. Each remainder condition must remain attached to its own original polynomial.

textbook_structural_branches.title: Recover coefficients from factor and remainder constraints

textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: The same coefficient occurs linearly and squared, producing a quadratic parameter equation and two admissible values p=2,4; this branch retention differs from the exam's unique solution of a linear system.

textbook_structural_branches.differing_decision: Here the divisor root and stated remainder both depend on the unknown a, so the conditions give two correlated nonlinear parameter branches. The exam has fixed divisor roots and a linear coefficient system.

For exam log(y)/log(5)=4log(5)/log(y), cross multiplication gives(log y)²=4(log5)², so both signed log values survive and y=25 or1/25 (y>0, y!=1). Goldie2B10(ii) instead needs three-term quadratic factorisation, rejects the negative root of positive 5^x, and takes logs to recover x. use trigonometrical identities for the simplification and exact evaluation of expressions and in the 
course of solving equations, and select an identity or identities appropriate to the context, 
showing familiarity in particular with the use of: 
- sec2θ  ≡ 1 + tan2θ and cosec2θ ≡ 1 + cot2θ , 
- the expansions of sin(A ± B), cos(A ± B) and tan(A ± B), 
- the formulae for sin2A, cos2A and tan2A, 
- the expressions a sinθ + b cosθ, a sinθ – b cosθ and a cosθ – b sinθ in the forms Rsin(θ ± α) 
and Rcos(θ ± α)

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Convert a linear sine/cosine combination to the prescribed R-form
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Both convert equal positive sine/cosine coefficients to Rcos(theta-alpha), choose the positive amplitude and acute phase, and return that form. The source coefficients 1,1 are scaled to 3,3 in the exam.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Convert a linear sine/cosine combination to the prescribed R-form
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: The source and exam use the same expression 2sin(theta)+sqrt(5)cos(theta) and the same Rsin(theta+alpha) template. Compare coefficients, obtain R and the acute phase to the requested precision.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Convert a linear sine/cosine combination to the prescribed R-form
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Both convert a positive cosine coefficient minus a positive sine coefficient to Rcos(theta+alpha). Coefficient values and requested rounding change; coefficient matching and phase sign decisions remain the same.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Convert to R-form then solve the original one-cycle equation
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Both selected conversion parts compare positive sine/cosine coefficients in Rcos(x-alpha); exact R and the acute rounded phase are the requested outputs.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Convert to R-form then solve the original one-cycle equation
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Both selected (a) parts convert positive sine/cosine sums to Rsin(theta+alpha), using coefficient comparison and an acute phase. The later solve responses are not part of this conversion match.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Convert to R-form then solve the original one-cycle equation
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Both selected (i)/(a) parts convert cosine minus sine to Rcos(theta+alpha), returning amplitude and acute phase. The coefficient values and phase precision vary.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Reduce an original reciprocal expression before R-form solving
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: The selected source (b) uses the linear combination already established in (a) to find Rsin(theta+alpha). Its reciprocal simplification and later roots are outside this conversion-only match.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Use an R-form in a changed multiple-angle equation
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: The selected source (a) converts 3cos(theta)-sin(theta) to Rcos(theta+alpha), exactly the same conversion decision as the exam with changed coefficients. The doubled-angle source solve part (b) is not included.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Use R-form for extrema, sketch and bounded solving
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: The selected conversion parts compare sine/cosine coefficients in an Rsin(argument+alpha) template. The source argument is 2theta instead of theta; its frequency does not change the coefficient-matching response in this selected part.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Use R-form for extrema, sketch and bounded solving
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Both selected parts use the earlier amplitude to state the attained maximum and minimum of a linear sine/cosine combination. Neither selected response asks for the angles where they occur.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Use R-form for extrema, sketch and bounded solving
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Both selected conversion parts transform positive cosine minus positive sine into Rcos(theta+alpha), returning the amplitude and acute phase. Only numerical coefficients and rounding differ.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Find extrema and the requested attaining arguments
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Match the sine and cosine coefficients, obtain positive R and the correct phase, in degrees to the stated precision. Only the selected R/phase response is linked, not later extrema.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Find extrema and the requested attaining arguments
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: The selected (a) source and exam both convert cosine minus sine into Rcos(theta+alpha), give positive R and acute alpha, and return the requested precision. The later extremum-argument response is excluded.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Find extrema and the requested attaining arguments
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Both selected responses state the maximum and minimum ordinates from the known amplitude. The source angle answers are expressly excluded.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Find extrema of a transformed linear trig combination
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Both selected conversion responses find positive R and acute phase in Rsin(theta+alpha); nonlinear source subparts are not included.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Find extrema of a transformed linear trig combination
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: The selected source (a) only gives the original linear combination extrema, so it matches the exam ordinate response. The shifted/squared/cubed source transforms are excluded.

same_type_textbook_practice.title: Use an R form to state extreme values without solving their angles
same_type_textbook_practice.comparison_evidence: Both selected (a) parts convert cosine minus sine to Rcos(theta+alpha). The scaled minimum in source (b) is not part of this match.
